name: OBD-II (SAE J1962)
description: The 16-pin diagnostic connector mandated on OBD-II vehicles (US cars and light trucks since 1996). Pin functions depend on which protocol the vehicle speaks; modern vehicles use ISO 15765-4 (CAN) on pins 6 and 14. Always powered from pin 16 (+12 V battery) with grounds on 4 and 5.

contacts.description: manufacturer discretionary (often GMLAN / SWCAN, or unused)

contacts.name: J1850+
contacts.description: J1850 PWM/VPW Bus+ (Ford/GM legacy); unused on CAN-only vehicles

contacts.name: CAN-H
contacts.description: CAN High -- the primary diagnostics bus on modern vehicles, ~2.5 V idle

contacts.name: K-line
contacts.description: K-line (KWP2000 / ISO 9141) serial init line; unused on CAN-only vehicles

contacts.name: J1850-
contacts.description: J1850 PWM Bus- (PWM only; VPW does not use it)

contacts.name: CAN-L
contacts.description: CAN Low -- pairs with pin 6, ~2.5 V idle, falls on dominant bits

contacts.name: +12V
contacts.description: unswitched +12 V battery (permanent power) -- the diagnostic tool's supply

variants: Type A: 12 V systems (passenger cars). Full-height center key.
Type B: 24 V systems (medium/heavy trucks). The center key has a wider, interrupted slot so a Type-A plug will not seat -- but a Type-B tool DOES fit a Type-A socket.
Pinout is protocol-dependent: CAN (6 & 14), J1850 PWM (2 & 10) or VPW (2), ISO 9141 / KWP (7, sometimes 15). On anything since ~2008, pins 6/14 (CAN) are what you want.
gotchas: Pins 6 (CAN-H) and 14 (CAN-L) ARE the CAN bus. To sniff a car or an OBD-II simulator you tap those two plus a ground; everything else is legacy or manufacturer-specific.
Pin 16 is ALWAYS-ON +12 V straight from the battery, not switched by the ignition -- a shorted tool or adapter can drain the battery or pop a fuse.

Both CAN lines rest near 2.5 V (recessive idle); do not expect 0 V. CAN-H rises and CAN-L falls together only during dominant bits, so a multimeter shows ~2.5 V DC with a small AC flicker under traffic.
A J1939 heavy truck uses a 9-pin Deutsch connector, NOT this J1962 -- entirely different pinout. Match the connector to the standard the sim/vehicle actually speaks.
There is no standard 5 V logic rail here. The tool powers itself from pin 16; your CAN transceiver's logic level comes from your own circuit, not the connector.
notes: Pinout per SAE J1962 and the ISO 15765-4 CAN pin assignment. Manufacturer-discretionary pins (1, 3, 8, 9, 11-13) vary by make; the CAN (6/14), power (16), and ground (4/5) pins are fixed by the standard.
